tldr: This is a loose topic cluster, not one event: three unrelated items about running inference on GPUs. Its main thread is AWS adding ways to share one GPU, starting with NVIDIA Multi-Instance GPU partitions for SageMaker endpoints on Nov 6.
whats_new: AWS Lambda now runs GPU inference on EC2 G-series instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU and vLLM/SGLang base images.
why_it_matters: Two AWS launches in three weeks move GPU sharing into managed services, so small or bursty models no longer need a dedicated, mostly idle GPU endpoint.

beats.headline: SageMaker endpoints can split one GPU with NVIDIA MIG
beats.summary: Hardware-isolated partitions let one GPU host several models or a right-sized slice for one.

beats.headline: Hobby project: a Windows Vulkan GGUF engine written in Delphi
beats.summary: A Hacker News item on local inference, unrelated to the managed-service thread.

beats.headline: Lambda runs GPU inference with 48 concurrent invocations per model
beats.summary: Lambda Managed Instances on G-series GPUs share one loaded model across invocations, with vLLM and SGLang base images.

open_questions: Which G-series instance types and regions does Lambda GPU support at launch?
How does Lambda GPU pricing compare with a SageMaker endpoint on a MIG partition for the same model?
What cold-start time does a Lambda GPU function show when it loads a model?
Does SageMaker MIG support cover all MIG profiles, or only a fixed set of partition sizes?
take_for_builders: If you run small or bursty models on dedicated GPU endpoints, benchmark the same model on a SageMaker MIG partition and on Lambda GPU before your next capacity renewal.
